Para a FAA, spray e gotas em geral não p: According to the FAA, sprays and drops usually do not protect enough, and oral decongestants can significantly impair performance.
Para a ICAO, o tímpano pode romper com 2: According to ICAO, the eardrum can rupture with a 200 to 500 mmHg difference; descending from 6,500 ft to sea level already gives about 150 mmHg.
Para o **passageiro**, a regra é a mesma: For **passengers**, the rule is the same as for the ear: with a sinus infection or severe congestion, they can **postpone** the flight and use a decongestant for relief. For **crew**, ANAC requires a **clear nose** and **no serious sinus disease**, with a sinus **X-ray** at the initial exam; ICAO requires no nasal obstruction. A cold is reassessed in **7 to 10 days**, and nobody flies with one.
Para o **passageiro**, o barotrauma em g: For **passengers**, barotrauma is usually not serious. Those with an **ear, nose or sinus infection** or **severe congestion** may **postpone the flight** to avoid pain and injury. For **crew**, the signs and symptoms of barotrauma **are not compatible with flying**: they return only after the acute process has fully passed and the eardrum examination is normal. A cold should be reassessed in **7 to 10 days**.
Para o **tripulante**, a ANAC e a ICAO u: For **crew**, ANAC and ICAO use **pure-tone audiometry**: up to **35 dB** at 500, 1,000 and 2,000 Hz and up to **50 dB** at 3,000 Hz, **in each ear**. At ANAC, the test is done every **5 years** under 40 and every **2 years** from 40. The FAA accepts hearing a **conversational voice at 1.8 m**, back turned, or a better-ear and worse-ear table. Anyone above the limit may still be fit if they **understand speech in cockpit noise**, in a special test or in flight. At ANAC, anyone failing in both ears is restricted from **using the radio** and from working as **cabin crew**.
Para o **tripulante**, a ANAC exige dent: For **crew**, ANAC requires enough teeth to chew without symptoms, **no deep decay**, gum or root disease, **no dental dressing** and **no root canal treatment in progress**, with a dental chart every **5 years** and a panoramic X-ray at the initial exam. Flying with barodontalgia means flying with pain that can **distract** or **incapacitate** on descent.
Para o **tripulante**: a ICAO e a ANAC e: For **crew**: ICAO and ANAC require no **vestibular disorder**, no **significant tube dysfunction** and no **unhealed perforation**; a **single dry perforation** does not make unfit, provided hearing meets the requirement. At ANAC, a **permanent** vestibular disorder makes unfit, and a **transient** one does until the condition recovers. After **stapedectomy**, ICAO asks for **1 to 3 months without flying**, specialist assessment and then flying restricted to **multi-crew for 2 years**. **Tympanoplasty** with an intact eardrum and normal hearing leaves no restriction. At the FAA, a **resolved** perforation without symptoms allows issuing the certificate, and ear surgery is decided by the FAA itself with the surgeon's report; **transient** vertigo, such as acute labyrinthitis or benign positional vertigo, may not disqualify after full recovery.
Para voar, é preciso **entender a fala e: To fly, you need to **understand speech and the radio** in cockpit noise, hear **warning signals** and the sounds of the aircraft itself. Speech is concentrated between **500 and 3,000 Hz**, and that is the range in which authorities measure hearing. Loss can be **conductive**, in the outer and middle ear, or **sensorineural**, in the inner ear and nerve; **presbycusis**, age-related loss, can begin after **30** and affects high-pitched sounds first.

Quando a pessoa não consegue equalizar n: When someone cannot equalize on descent, deafness, tinnitus and pain come quickly. If the tube stays closed, the air in the middle ear is absorbed and **fluid** comes in: this is **serous otitis media**, with an amber eardrum and sometimes a fluid line. In rare, severe cases, pressure ruptures the **round or oval window** of the inner ear, with **severe vertigo** and hearing loss: this is **inner ear barotrauma**. A sudden eardrum perforation on descent can also cause **alternobaric vertigo** and incapacitate the pilot.

Voar com sinusite é arriscar uma dor que: Flying with sinusitis risks pain that can **incapacitate** the pilot on approach. Secretion trapped in the blocked sinus favors **infection**. The pain usually eases within minutes with a **mild nasal vasoconstrictor**, but anyone on **antibiotics** or **antihistamines** does not fly during treatment.
Voar com uma vertigem ativa ou cedo dema: Flying with active vertigo or too soon after surgery risks **incapacitation** mid-descent. Anyone who had stapes surgery must know that **colds** and nasal infections threaten middle ear ventilation.
Voar ouvindo mal é arriscar **perder uma: Flying with poor hearing risks **missing an instruction** from control or an **alarm**. That is why hearing loss is followed with repeated audiograms. **Hearing aids** are generally **not accepted in flight** for professional crew, because the aircraft headset and intercom already fill that role; for others, only after assessment.
Voar resfriado é o caminho mais comum pa: Flying with a cold is the most common route to barotrauma. A pilot who disregards a cold risks **acute incapacitation** from ear or sinus pain and, in some cases, **irreversible vertigo and hearing loss**, which can ground them for good. Fluid that stays in the ear for weeks can also leave **permanent hearing loss**.
